summary: @onereach/si-root preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue `si-root` step-inputs component library (source shipped under `lib/`), but its `package.json` declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from oven-sh's GitHub release assets and then invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D })`, using the freshly downloaded alternate runtime to execute a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727,680-byte file sitting at the tarball root that is not listed in the `files` array (which only declares `lib/*`) and is heavily obfuscated with a rotating string-array cipher (`WV8StW` shift routine, ~1500-entry mixed hex/token array `n7gIxM`, `_0xNNNN`-style identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header indicating it is compiled specifically for the Bun runtime the preinstall step fetches). A Vue component library has no legitimate need for the Bun runtime nor for an undeclared 728KB obfuscated blob, and executing it via a non-Node runtime bypasses Node-based inspection. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: a lifecycle hook fetches an alien runtime specifically to run an opaque payload that mismatches the package's advertised purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
